# Runtime Features — Epic Intake Brief

## Headline

Group the outstanding ToneForge demo milestones (Demo 10–16) and the remaining
runtime-related work items into a single tracking epic, so the runtime roadmap can
be prioritised, sequenced by dependency, and driven to completion.

## Problem statement

The remaining runtime and roadmap work is currently spread across many standalone
items plus a partially-populated epic. The epic description was a single paragraph
with no success criteria, and its stated contents did not match its actual children
(the "machine-use demo" was referenced as a child but is unparented). This epic now
provides the grouping and dependency view, and its stated contents have been
reconciled with the actual child set.

## Users

- **ToneForge producers/maintainers** who need one place to track and prioritise the
  outstanding demo milestones and runtime enhancements.
- **Implementing engineers/agents** who need the group's boundary, dependency order,
  and definition of done.

Example user stories:

- As a producer, I want the remaining runtime/roadmap features grouped under one epic
  with explicit dependencies, so that I can see what is blocked and sequence work.
- As an engineer, I want each child of the epic to carry a clear goal and measurable
  acceptance criteria, so that I can pick up a child and know when it is done.
- As a maintainer, I want the runtime module to eventually produce audible output in
  a meaningful demo, so that the runtime's value is demonstrable end-to-end.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every direct child of this epic reaches a terminal stage (`in_review` or
   `completed`); the epic itself is advanced to `in_review` only once all children
   are terminal and blockers are resolved.
2. Each direct child has a clear goal and measurable acceptance criteria, verified by
   the shared tree-coverage review (`run_coverage_review`) returning `proceed` for the
   epic.
3. Inter-child dependency edges are recorded via `wl dep` and honoured in execution
   order (prerequisites first, per `docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md`).
4. The runtime PRD revisit (TF-0MM4M1NXU0WHH6AJ) is resolved: `docs/prd/RUNTIME_PRD.md`
   defines how the runtime wires into the render/playback pipeline, and the resulting
   audio-producing runtime demo has a clear, verifiable audible-output user story.
5. The epic's child inventory accurately reflects its actual children (no phantom
   entries; any item referenced as a child must genuinely be parented to this epic).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code
   comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Scope

**In scope**

- Grouping and dependency maintenance for Demo 10–16 and the runtime enhancements
  listed as children.
- Resolving the runtime PRD revisit and defining the audio-producing runtime demo.
- Keeping the epic's stated contents aligned with its actual children.

**Out of scope**

- Implementing any child feature (each child owns its own implementation).
- New runtime/roadmap features not already represented by a child.
- Promotion to `main`/release (owned by the `ship` skill).

## Constraints

- Demo sequencing follows `docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md`; blocked children stay blocked
  until their prerequisites complete.
- The runtime PRD (`docs/prd/RUNTIME_PRD.md`) is authoritative for runtime behaviour;
  the epic must not invent behaviour that contradicts it.
- Manual/curated PRDs in `docs/prd/` are the source of product intent.
- Mixer rules are declarative JSON stored under `.toneforge/mixer/` (confirmed; see
  Appendix Q2.1), consistent with the existing `.toneforge/config.yaml` convention.

## Existing state

- Epic is `issueType: epic`, `priority: low`, assignee `Map`.
- 9 direct children and 5 grandchildren (under Demo 10 and Demo 13) exist (see
  disposition tables below); Demo 11–16 are `blocked` on prerequisites; the remaining
  direct children are `open`/`plan_complete`.
- `src/runtime/` orchestrates state/context/sequence presets but does not itself
  produce audio; the previous Demo 9 was removed for logging simulated transitions
  only.
- `README.md` and `docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md` describe the overall demo sequence.

### Child inventory & disposition

**Direct children (9)** — these define the epic's completion (AC 1):

| Child | Title | Status | Stage | Type | Disposition |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TF-0MLXF8ZW21HJLFOG | Demo 10: Mixer | open | plan_complete | epic | Planned; 3 children created |
| TF-0MLXF98WZ1LQGM5W | Demo 11: Intelligence | blocked | idea | epic | Well-defined; blocked on Demo 7 (complete) & Demo 10 |
| TF-0MLXF9FWG18T2ZHD | Demo 12: Compiler & Validator | blocked | idea | epic | Well-defined; blocked on Demo 7 (complete) & Demo 11 |
| TF-0MLXF9O241QG5APK | Demo 13: Visualizer & Haptics | blocked | idea | epic | Well-defined; blocked on Demo 9 (complete) & Demo 10 |
| TF-0MLXFB8R61P63G4B | Demo 14: Intent & Memory | blocked | idea | epic | Well-defined; blocked on Demo 11 |
| TF-0MLXFBHHW1BBO1ZJ | Demo 15: Network & Integrations | blocked | idea | epic | Well-defined; blocked on Demo 9 (complete) & Demo 12 |
| TF-0MLXFBLNF1MCYS6Y | Demo 16: Marketplace | blocked | idea | epic | Well-defined; blocked on Demo 12 & Demo 15 |
| TF-0MLYX9DP51U7AQDK | Realtime adjustment of parameters | blocked | plan_complete | feature | Planned; blocked on TF-0MM4M1NXU0WHH6AJ |
| TF-0MM4M1NXU0WHH6AJ | Revisit runtime PRD | open | plan_complete | task | Planned; ready to implement |

**Grandchildren (5)** — tracked through their parents, not direct children:

| Child | Title | Parent | Status | Stage |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TF-0MMLC8PXU0D3O594 | Mixer rule config loader | Demo 10 | open | plan_complete |
| TF-0MMLC8B3T0Z1F7ZM | Mixer runtime foundation | Demo 10 | blocked | plan_complete |
| TF-0MMLC8SQ302DVYOZ | Mixer voice limiting tests | Demo 10 | blocked | plan_complete |
| TF-0MMN7O97300JWHEW | Demo 13A: Visualizer | Demo 13 | blocked | intake_complete |
| TF-0MMN7O9901NGG0NA | Demo 13B: Haptics | Demo 13 | blocked | intake_complete |

> **Inventory correction (plan, 2026-10-06).** Earlier revisions stated "14 direct
> children" and listed 5 grandchildren (the three Mixer tasks and Demo 13A/13B) as
> direct children. The authoritative `parentId` values show **9 direct children**; the
> 5 others are parented to Demo 10 and Demo 13. Corrected to satisfy AC 5.

### Resolved discrepancies

- The description previously named **"the machine-use demo"** as a child, but
  TF-0MLYUG79Y1KMDPMI is unparented. Per producer decision (Appendix Q4) the
  description now references it only under Related work; it remains standalone.
- Blocked children (Demo 11–16) cannot be claimed for intake without erasing their
  `blocked` status, so their per-child intake pass cannot run until prerequisites
  complete. Their descriptions are already detailed.

## Desired change

- Finalise this epic's goal, users, success criteria, scope, and constraints as above.
- Child inventory reconciled with the actual children (AC 5).
- Per-child intake pass run for the four under-defined open children
  (the three Mixer tasks and "Realtime adjustment of parameters"); the well-defined
  open children auto-completed.
- **Planning pass (2026-10-06):** all resolvable open questions closed; open direct
  children and grandchildren advanced; dependency edges verified and completed;
  inventory corrected. See the "Plan" section below.

## Plan

Planning pass for this meta-epic (effort Extra Large, risk Medium; producer approved
2026-10-06).

**Outcome**

- All open questions closed (Appendix Q1–Q4); the dependency anomaly was resolved by
  producer decision (stale edge removed — see below).
- Direct children: 7 of 9 are `plan_complete`; the 6 blocked demo epics are
  well-defined and remain `idea` until their prerequisites complete.
- Dependency edges added (8 total):
  - `TF-0MMLC8B3T0Z1F7ZM` (Mixer runtime) → depends-on `TF-0MMLC8PXU0D3O594` (loader)
  - `TF-0MMLC8SQ302DVYOZ` (Mixer voice tests) → depends-on `TF-0MMLC8B3T0Z1F7ZM` and
    `TF-0MMLC8PXU0D3O594`
  - `TF-0MLYX9DP51U7AQDK` (Realtime adjustment) → depends-on `TF-0MM4M1NXU0WHH6AJ`
    (Revisit runtime PRD)
  - `TF-0MMN7O97300JWHEW` / `TF-0MMN7O9901NGG0NA` (Demo 13A/13B) → depends-on Demo 9
    (`TF-0MLXF8TBT0DJDCO1`) and Demo 10 (`TF-0MLXF8ZW21HJLFOG`)
- Inventory corrected (AC 5): 9 direct children, 5 grandchildren.
- Stale Mixer path `config/mixer/*.json` corrected to `.toneforge/mixer/*.json` in
  Demo 10's description (producer-confirmed, Appendix Q2.1).

**Execution order (unblocked work first)**

1. `TF-0MMLC8PXU0D3O594` Mixer rule config loader (no prerequisites)
2. `TF-0MMLC8B3T0Z1F7ZM` Mixer runtime foundation (after 1)
3. `TF-0MMLC8SQ302DVYOZ` Mixer voice limiting tests (after 1 and 2)
4. `TF-0MM4M1NXU0WHH6AJ` Revisit runtime PRD (no prerequisites)
5. `TF-0MLYX9DP51U7AQDK` Realtime adjustment of parameters (after 4)
6. Demo 11–16 unblock as their prerequisites complete, per `docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md`.

**Plan: Dependency anomaly — RESOLVED**

- Demo 13 (`TF-0MLXF9O241QG5APK`) had a stale `depends-on` edge to
  `TF-0MLYUG79Y1KMDPMI` "Machine use demo", contradicting
  `docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md` (Demo 13 prerequisites: 9, 10 only) and Appendix Q4.
  **Producer confirmed removal (2026-10-06)**; the edge has been removed. Demo 13 now
  depends only on Demo 9 (`TF-0MLXF8TBT0DJDCO1`, complete) and Demo 10
  (`TF-0MLXF8ZW21HJLFOG`).

**Plan: changelog**

- 2026-10-06 — `plan` skill: closed Appendix Q1–Q4 open questions; advanced the three
  Mixer children, Realtime adjustment and Revisit runtime PRD to `plan_complete`;
  corrected the Demo 10 rule path; corrected the epic inventory (AC 5); added 8
  dependency edges.
- 2026-10-06 — `plan` skill (producer-approved follow-up): removed the stale
  Demo 13 → "Machine use demo" dependency edge; no open questions remain.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md` — canonical demo sequence and dependencies.
- `docs/prd/RUNTIME_PRD.md` — runtime behaviour to be revisited by TF-0MM4M1NXU0WHH6AJ.
- `docs/prd/MIXER_PRD.md` — Mixer concepts underlying the Demo 10 children.
- `src/runtime/runtime.ts` — runtime module referenced by the PRD revisit.
- `.toneforge/mixer/*.json` — confirmed declarative Mixer rules location (Appendix Q2.1).
- `README.md` — roadmap/feature overview to keep in sync.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: scope creep.** Adding new runtime/roadmap features to this grouping epic
  expands it indefinitely. *Mitigation:* record any new opportunity as a separate work
  item (child if it blocks, otherwise `discovered-from`) rather than widening this epic.
- **Risk: phantom children / stale description** misleads prioritisation.
  *Mitigation:* reconcile the child inventory (AC 5) — done in this intake.
- **Risk: blocked children are intake'd prematurely**, erasing `blocked` status.
  *Mitigation:* only intake blocked children after prerequisites complete.
- **Assumption:** the epic's purpose is tracking/grouping (meta-epic), not delivering a
  single new capability; completion is defined by its children reaching terminal stage.
- **Assumption:** Mixer rules are behavioural config under `.toneforge/mixer/*.json`,
  not sound-content presets (confirmed, Appendix Q2.1).

## Related work (manual)

- `docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md` — the demo sequence this epic tracks.
- TF-0MUUB39EL000YCT0 "Make ToneForge Runtime-aware (browser-compatible playback)"
  (`in-progress`, `in_review`) — directly advances runtime playback; not currently a
  child of this epic.
- TF-0MUV748IA0028PVO "Browser e2e: pre-existing terminal/wizard failures"
  (`in-progress`) — related browser demo/reliability work.
- TF-0MLYUG79Y1KMDPMI "Machine use demo" — standalone CLI JSON-reporting demo,
  intentionally not a child of this epic (Appendix Q4).
- TF-0MLXF8TBT0DJDCO1 "Demo 9: Runtime & State" (`completed`) — prerequisite of
  Demo 10/13/15, and the source of the runtime PRD revisit item.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (epic definition).** How should this grouping epic measure success?
  - Options: (A) Meta-epic — success = every child reaches a terminal stage;
    (B) Deliverable epic — owns a concrete runtime deliverable beyond its children.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply): A.**
  - Rationale: the item is framed as an epic *grouping*; AC 4 binds the one concrete
    outcome (the runtime PRD revisit) without duplicating a child.

- **Q2 (Demo 10 / Mixer children).** Three questions left open by the prior Demo 10
  intake.
  - **Q2.1** Confirm the rules file path.
    - Options considered: (A) `config/mixer/*.json`; (B) `presets/mixer/*.json`;
      (C) `.toneforge/mixer/*.json`.
    - **Answer (producer, interactive reply): C.**
    - Rationale: `.toneforge/` already holds project config (`.toneforge/config.yaml`,
      loaded in `src/classify/dimensions/category.ts`); Mixer rules are behavioural
      config, not sound content. `config/` has no precedent in this repo.
  - **Q2.2** Confirm the mix group list.
    - **Answer (resolved from repo evidence, no producer input required):**
      footsteps, UI, combat, ambience, dialogue, alerts — listed verbatim in
      `docs/prd/MIXER_PRD.md` §4.1.
  - **Q2.3** Add Demo 9 (Runtime & State) as a blocking dependency now?
    - **Answer (resolved from repo evidence):** already recorded — `wl dep list
      TF-0MLXF8ZW21HJLFOG` shows an outbound `depends-on` on TF-0MLXF8TBT0DJDCO1
      (Demo 9). No action needed.

- **Q3 ("Realtime adjustment of parameters", TF-0MLYX9DP51U7AQDK).** What is the
  intended scope?
  - Options: (A) real-time modulation of a specific parameter set (e.g. engine
    RPM/pitch) for continuous sounds only; (B) general real-time parameter automation
    for any playing sound; (C) out of scope for this epic.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply): A.**
  - Rationale: `CORE_PRD.md` §6.5 designs vehicle engines as loop + LFO pitch
    modulation; `RUNTIME_PRD.md` §6 defines `setSfxParameter(id, name, value)`, while
    general "Runtime parameter automation" is listed as a Future Extension (§16).

- **Q4 (child reconciliation).** The description listed "the machine-use demo" as a
  child, but TF-0MLYUG79Y1KMDPMI is unparented.
  - Options: (A) re-parent it under this epic; (B) correct the description and keep it
    standalone.
  - **Answer (producer, interactive reply): B.**
  - Rationale: it is a self-contained CLI JSON-reporting demo (already
    `intake_complete`) and not runtime/demo-roadmap work; it is preserved under
    Related work.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **TF-0MLXF8TBT0DJDCO1** – Demo 9: Runtime & State -- Real-Time Behavioral Sound (completed)
- **TF-0MMJVDBHQ0YWQBY2** – Remove archived legacy CLI core (cleanup) (completed)
- **TF-0MM0AJYOF1HKBKMG** – Intensity Dimension Classifier (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md` — matched: acceptance, action, add, aligned, already (+190 more)
- `standups/2026_10_05.md` — matched: action, actual, add, adding, already (+188 more)
- `docs/prd/BRAINSTORM_QUESTIONS.md` — matched: action, actual, assumption, assumptions, audio (+105 more)

# Marketplace registry abstraction, local adapter and search

## Goal

Provide the injectable registry abstraction (Assumption A1: local/offline adapter behind
an interface, remote adapter deferred to Demo 15) and deterministic, metadata-rich
category search (`docs/prd/MARKETPLACE_PRD.md` Sections 10, 12, 14).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A `MarketplaceRegistry` interface supports package search and fetch; the local
   adapter reads a directory/fixture registry with no network access.
2. `search(category)` returns listings with `name@version`, author, contained asset
   counts (recipes, stacks, sequences, palettes), rating and license.
3. Identical registry state yields identical result ordering; a `--json`-ready result
   shape is exposed.
4. Unit tests cover the local adapter and search determinism and precede the
   implementation.

## Minimal Implementation

- `src/marketplace/registry.ts`: interface + local directory-backed adapter, injected
  into callers (no globals).
- `src/marketplace/search.ts`: category filtering and deterministic ordering.
- `src/marketplace/search.test.ts`: tests written first, using F1 fixtures.

## Key Files:

- `src/marketplace/registry.ts`
- `src/marketplace/search.ts`
- `src/marketplace/search.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Registry interface + local adapter.
- Deterministic category search.
- Unit tests.

## Dependencies

- F1 (Marketplace conformance harness and fixture registry).
- F2 (Package manifest types and schema validation).
data.title: Marketplace registry abstraction, local adapter and search

# Semver and dependency conflict detection

## Goal

Enforce semantic versioning and detect version conflicts with actionable errors so a
dependency bump cannot silently break builds (`docs/prd/MARKETPLACE_PRD.md` Sections 5,
9, 11).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Semver parsing, comparison and range compatibility are implemented (or delegated to a
   vetted minimal implementation) without adding an unjustified runtime dependency.
2. Missing, circular and incompatible-major dependencies each produce a distinct,
   actionable structured error.
3. Resolution is deterministic and independent of input ordering.
4. Unit tests cover each conflict class and the compatible case and precede the
   implementation.

## Minimal Implementation

- `src/marketplace/version.ts`: semver helpers plus dependency resolution and conflict
  classification.
- `src/marketplace/version.test.ts`: tests written first, using F1 fixtures.
- Prefer a small in-repo implementation over a new dependency (`package.json` currently
  has no semver library).

## Key Files:

- `src/marketplace/version.ts`
- `src/marketplace/version.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Semver + dependency resolution helpers.
- Structured conflict errors.
- Unit tests.

## Dependencies

- F1 (Marketplace conformance harness and fixture registry).
- F2 (Package manifest types and schema validation).
data.title: Semver and dependency conflict detection

# Marketplace install pipeline

## Goal

Deliver `install(package@version)` end-to-end: fetch -> integrity check -> validate ->
register assets -> version lock + provenance (`docs/prd/MARKETPLACE_PRD.md` Sections 7,
8.1, 10).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Install fetches from the registry, verifies content-hash integrity, validates the
   manifest and delegates to the Demo 12 Validator.
2. Invalid packages and integrity failures are rejected **before** any local
   registration occurs.
3. A successful install registers recipes/stacks/sequences/palettes, records provenance
   and locks the exact version.
4. Re-installing the same version is reproducible (identical registered state and
   byte-identical outputs).
5. Unit and integration tests use the fixture registry only (no live network).

## Minimal Implementation

- `src/marketplace/install.ts`: orchestrate the pipeline against the F3 registry and F4
  resolver, delegating the quality gate to the Demo 12 Validator interface.
- `src/marketplace/install.test.ts`: tests written first; failure paths before success.
- Registration into the library/recipe registry is completed by F8.

## Key Files:

- `src/marketplace/install.ts`
- `src/marketplace/install.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Install pipeline with integrity, validation, version lock and provenance.
- Unit + integration tests.

## Dependencies

- F1 (Marketplace conformance harness and fixture registry).
- F2 (Package manifest types and schema validation).
- F3 (Marketplace registry abstraction, local adapter and search).
- F4 (Semver and dependency conflict detection).
- Demo 12 Compiler & Validator (`TF-0MLXF9FWG18T2ZHD`) supplies the Validator gate.
data.title: Marketplace install pipeline

# Marketplace publish pipeline with Validator gate

## Goal

Deliver `publish(packageDir, name, version)` that validates a package (including the
Demo 12 Validator), rejects invalid packages with structured errors, and publishes
immutably (`docs/prd/MARKETPLACE_PRD.md` Sections 7, 9).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Publish validates manifest/schema, dependency resolution, determinism checks, license
   declaration and delegates to the Demo 12 Validator.
2. Invalid packages are rejected with structured errors and nothing is published.
3. Published versions are immutable; republishing an existing version fails with an
   actionable error.
4. Unit tests cover the reject and publish paths via the fixture registry.

## Minimal Implementation

- `src/marketplace/publish.ts`: validation orchestration + immutable write to the
  registry adapter, delegating the quality gate to the Demo 12 Validator interface.
- `src/marketplace/publish.test.ts`: tests written first; rejection paths before success.

## Key Files:

- `src/marketplace/publish.ts`
- `src/marketplace/publish.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Publish pipeline with Validator gate and immutability.
- Structured rejection errors.
- Unit tests.

## Dependencies

- F1 (Marketplace conformance harness and fixture registry).
- F2 (Package manifest types and schema validation).
- F4 (Semver and dependency conflict detection).
- Demo 12 Compiler & Validator (`TF-0MLXF9FWG18T2ZHD`) supplies the Validator gate.
data.title: Marketplace publish pipeline with Validator gate

# Marketplace CLI command group

## Goal

Expose the Marketplace through a `marketplace` command group registered in the yargs CLI,
with the documented `--json` contracts (`docs/prd/DEMO_ROADMAP.md` Demo 16).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `toneforge marketplace search --category <c>` returns listings and supports `--json`.
2. `toneforge marketplace install <package>@<version>` installs and reports the
   registered assets, and supports `--json`.
3. `toneforge marketplace publish --package <dir> --name <n> --version <v>` validates
   and publishes, and supports `--json`.
4. The `marketplace` group is registered in `src/cli.yargs.ts` and appears in CLI help.
5. CLI integration tests cover all three commands and their `--json` contracts.

## Minimal Implementation

- `src/cli/commands/marketplace.ts`: command module following the
  `src/cli/commands/library.ts` pattern.
- `src/cli.yargs.ts`: register the group.
- `src/cli.marketplace.integration.test.ts`: tests written first against the fixture
  registry.

## Key Files:

- `src/cli/commands/marketplace.ts`
- `src/cli.yargs.ts`
- `src/cli.marketplace.integration.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Marketplace CLI group (search/install/publish) with `--json`.
- CLI integration tests.

## Dependencies

- F3 (Marketplace registry abstraction, local adapter and search).
- F5 (Marketplace install pipeline).
- F6 (Marketplace publish pipeline with Validator gate).

# Register installed assets into library and recipe registry

## Goal

Make installed marketplace assets usable immediately by registering them through the
existing library index store and recipe registry rather than a forked store
(`docs/prd/MARKETPLACE_PRD.md` Sections 8.1, 10).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Installed recipes are available immediately via
   `toneforge generate --recipe <installed>`.
2. Installed stacks render via `toneforge stack render`.
3. Registration reuses the existing `src/library/` index store and
   `src/core/recipe.ts` registry (extend, do not fork), plus Demo 7 conventions where
   present.
4. An installed asset produces byte-identical output to an equivalent locally authored
   asset for the same seed.
5. Integration tests cover `generate` and `stack render` against a fixture install.

## Minimal Implementation

- Extend `src/library/index-store.ts` and `src/core/recipe.ts` registration helpers as
  needed.
- Wire registration from `src/marketplace/install.ts` into the existing registry.
- `src/marketplace/install.integration.test.ts`: tests written first.

## Key Files:

- `src/library/index-store.ts`
- `src/core/recipe.ts`
- `src/marketplace/install.ts`
- `src/marketplace/install.integration.test.ts`

## Deliverables

- Installed assets registered into the local registry.
- Determinism integration tests.

## Dependencies

- F5 (Marketplace install pipeline).

## Goal

Test-first foundation for the Integrations module: an offline fixture library and
conformance harness that exercises generate -> validate -> compile -> export and asserts
deterministic, platform-appropriate output.

## What the user sees

The integrations conformance suite runs the full pipeline against fixtures offline and
asserts the produced file structures and manifests.

## Minimal implementation

- Fixture library + harness under `src/test-utils/fixtures/integrations/valid-library/library.json`.
- Golden assertions on output directory structure and `manifest.json` contents.
- A negative fixture (invalid library) asserting structured validation failure.

## Key Files

- `src/integrations/__tests__/conformance.test.ts` — New: pipeline conformance tests.
- `src/test-utils/fixtures/integrations/valid-library/library.json` — New: valid/invalid fixture libraries.
- `docs/prd/INTEGRATIONS_PRD.md` — Sections 4.2, 7, 9 (CI, determinism, sync).

## Constraints

- Offline and deterministic; no network, no system audio player.
- Reuse existing compiler/validator fixtures and CLI test helpers where possible.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A fixture library and harness under `src/test-utils/fixtures/integrations/valid-library/library.json` runs the
   four pipeline stages (generate, validate, compile, export) offline.
2. Golden assertions cover output file structure and manifest contents; output is
   deterministic across runs.
3. A negative fixture (invalid library) asserts validation fails with structured errors.
4. Tests are included in `npm test`, offline and deterministic.
5. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Risky assumptions

- The integrations module can be exercised purely through the CLI; if a library API is
  needed, it is exported and tested directly too.

## Goal

Define the versioned behavioural event (identifier, seed, timestamp, state snapshot,
context snapshot) and its canonical serialization, shared by host and clients.

## What the user sees

A documented event type that serializes to a compact canonical form and round-trips
exactly; unknown event versions are rejected gracefully.

## Minimal implementation

- `BehaviouralEvent` types + validation (`event`, `seed`, `time`, `state`, `context`).
- Canonical, deterministic encode/decode (stable key order) with a version field.
- Forward-compatible dispatch: unknown versions are skipped with a structured warning.
- Unit tests for round-trip, malformed input and unknown version.

## Key Files

- `src/network/types.ts` — New: behavioural event and snapshot types.
- `src/network/events.ts` — New: canonical serialization + version handling.
- `src/network/__tests__/events.test.ts` — New: unit tests.
- `docs/prd/NETWORK_PRD.md` — Sections 4.1, 7 (event shape, API).

## Constraints

- No new runtime dependency for serialization (use JSON with canonical key ordering).
- Events are compact: keep the encoded form bounded and documented.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Types and validation for the behavioural event match `docs/prd/NETWORK_PRD.md`
   Section 4.1.
2. Canonical serialization is deterministic (stable ordering) and round-trips exactly.
3. Events are versioned; unknown versions are rejected or skipped gracefully without
   crashing.
4. Unit tests cover round-trip, malformed input, and unknown-version handling.
5. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Risky assumptions

- Downstream consumers only need the fields in NETWORK_PRD Section 4.1; further fields
  are additive and version-gated.
data.title: Behavioral event model and canonical serialization

## Goal

Implement transport-agnostic host/join and broadcast for behavioural events, with a
WebSocket adapter that reuses the existing `ws` dependency, under a host-authoritative
model for the demo.

## What the user sees

`network.host({ port })` starts a host session; `network.join("host:port")` connects a
client; the host broadcasts state changes and each peer receives them in a deterministic
order.

## Minimal implementation

- Transport interface with an in-memory adapter (tests) and a WebSocket adapter (runtime).
- `host()` / `join()` session lifecycle + peer registry (connect/disconnect).
- Host-authoritative broadcast of behavioural events; non-host peers relay only.
- Tests use the in-memory adapter; one integration test exercises the WebSocket adapter.

## Key Files

- `src/network/session.ts` — New: host/join lifecycle, peer registry, authority.
- `src/network/transport.ts` — New: transport interface + in-memory adapter.
- `src/network/ws-transport.ts` — New: WebSocket adapter (reuses `ws`).
- `src/network/index.ts` — New: public module surface.
- `docs/prd/NETWORK_PRD.md` — Sections 4.3, 7 (authority, API).

## Constraints

- Reuse the existing `ws` dependency (already used by `web/server`); add no new runtime
  dependency.
- The core must not depend on the WebSocket implementation (injectable transport).
- No live network in unit tests.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `network.host()` starts a host session and `network.join()` connects a client, with
   connection lifecycle events emitted.
2. The host broadcasts behavioural events to all connected peers; a peer receives them in
   deterministic order.
3. Authority is host-authoritative and documented; non-host peers do not emit
   authoritative events.
4. The peer registry tracks connect/disconnect and removes dropped peers.
5. Tests use an in-memory adapter plus one WebSocket integration test; full project test
   suite passes.

## Risky assumptions

- Browser WebSocket client support is sufficient for the demo (no Node-only transport
  needed in the browser).
data.title: Network transport: host/join, broadcast, authority

## Goal

Provide an engine-adapter interface that maps ToneForge categories to engine audio groups
and tags to mixer buses, with Unity and web adapters, exposed through
`toneforge sync --target <engine> --library <path> --output <path>`.

## What the user sees

`toneforge sync --target unity --library ./library --output ./unity-project/Assets/Audio/`
writes WAV files under `Assets/Audio/<category>/` plus a `manifest.json` mapping categories
to Unity audio groups/mixer buses. `--target web` writes a web-appropriate structure.

## Minimal implementation

- Adapter interface (`EngineAdapter`) + registry keyed by target name.
- Unity adapter (category -> audio group / mixer bus, `Assets/Audio/<category>/` layout).
- Web adapter (platform-appropriate flat/manifest layout).
- `sync` CLI command registered in `src/cli.yargs.ts`, with `--json` output.
- Deterministic, idempotent output; structured error for unsupported targets.

## Key Files

- `src/integrations/adapter.ts` — New: adapter interface + registry.
- `src/integrations/unity.ts` — New: Unity adapter and metadata mapping.
- `src/integrations/web.ts` — New: web adapter.
- `src/integrations/index.ts` — New: public module surface.
- `src/cli/commands/sync.ts` — New: `sync` command.
- `src/cli.yargs.ts` — Register the `sync` framework command.
- `docs/prd/INTEGRATIONS_PRD.md` — Sections 4.1, 5.1, 6, 9 (targets, CLI, mapping, sync).

## Constraints

- Reuse the Demo 12 Compiler output and Validator; do not re-implement compile/validate.
- Deterministic, reproducible output; safe for CI.
- TypeScript strict; `npm run typecheck` and `npm test` stay green.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `toneforge sync --target unity --library <path> --output <path>` produces
   `Assets/Audio/<category>/<name>.wav` plus a `manifest.json` mapping categories to
   audio groups/mixer buses - parent AC4.
2. `--target web` produces a platform-appropriate file structure.
3. Output is deterministic and idempotent (re-running yields byte-identical output).
4. An unsupported target fails with a structured, actionable error.
5. Unit and CLI integration tests cover both targets; full project test suite passes.

## Risky assumptions

- Unity audio-group/mixer-bus mapping is metadata-only in this demo (no Unity project
  files are generated beyond the audio folder + manifest).

## Goal

Late-joining clients receive a state snapshot and converge to the live state, with
timestamp correction and bounded drift compensation under jitter.

## What the user sees

A client that joins after playback has started receives a snapshot, immediately plays the
correct current output, and stays aligned as further transitions arrive.

## Minimal implementation

- Snapshot request/response on join (current state + context + seed).
- Timestamp correction and ordering for out-of-order/late events.
- Bounded drift compensation with documented tolerance and graceful degradation.
- Tests for late join, reordered delivery and simulated jitter using the harness.

## Key Files

- `src/network/snapshot.ts` — New: snapshot capture/apply on join.
- `src/network/sync.ts` — New: timestamp correction, ordering, drift compensation.
- `src/network/__tests__/sync.test.ts` — New: late-join/reorder/jitter tests.
- `docs/prd/NETWORK_PRD.md` — Section 8 (latency and drift handling).

## Constraints

- Bounded divergence: drift compensation must never cause unbounded state jumps.
- Deterministic given the same delivered event order.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. On join, the host sends a state snapshot and the late joiner resolves the current state
   and plays the correct deterministic output (parent AC5).
2. Out-of-order/late events are ordered by timestamp; drift compensation is bounded and
   documented.
3. Under simulated jitter the two clients remain aligned within a documented tolerance
   (harness assertion).
4. Tests cover late join, reordering and jitter; full project test suite passes.

## Risky assumptions

- The demo tolerance for perceptual alignment can be expressed in the resolved-output
  descriptor; if not, a documented fallback threshold is used.
data.title: Late-join snapshot and drift/latency handling

## Goal

Provide a non-interactive CI pipeline orchestration that generates, validates, compiles
and exports sounds in one deterministic run, with structured logs and exit codes.

## What the user sees

A single CI-style command/script runs generate -> validate -> compile -> export without
manual intervention and fails the build on any stage error; an example CI workflow
documents usage.

## Minimal implementation

- Orchestration entry point chaining the existing `generate`, `validate`, `compile` and
  `sync`/export stages (reuse the CLI/core modules; no duplication).
- Structured (JSON) stage logs and non-zero exit on failure.
- Example GitHub Actions workflow under `.github/workflows/` or `docs/guides/`.
- Offline conformance test covering success and a failing stage.

## Key Files

- `src/integrations/pipeline.ts` — New: pipeline orchestration.
- `src/cli/commands/sync.ts` / a pipeline entry point — wire the non-interactive run.
- `docs/guides/ci-integration.md` — New: CI guide + example workflow.
- `docs/prd/INTEGRATIONS_PRD.md` — Sections 4.2, 7, 10 (CI, determinism, validation).

## Constraints

- Non-interactive by default; safe for CI (no prompts, explicit file access).
- Reuse generate/validate/compile/sync; do not re-implement them.
- Deterministic; no live network.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A single non-interactive run executes generate -> validate -> compile -> export and
   exits non-zero if any stage fails - parent AC3.
2. It emits structured (JSON) logs suitable for CI.
3. An example CI workflow documents the pipeline.
4. An offline conformance test covers both the success path and a failing-stage path.
5. Full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Risky assumptions

- GitHub Actions is an acceptable example CI platform; the pipeline itself stays
  platform-neutral.
data.title: CI pipeline orchestration (generate -> validate -> compile -> export)

## Goal

Wire received behavioural events into the Demo 9 runtime/state pipeline so that two
clients play deterministically identical audio, and demonstrate the bandwidth proof in a
two-window browser demo.

## What the user sees

Two browser windows side by side: the host changes state (`walk` -> `run`) and both windows
play deterministically identical audio; the network payload is behavioural events, not
audio.

## Minimal implementation

- Adapter from received behavioural events to the runtime/state API (reuse Demo 9;
  do not fork runtime logic).
- Two-window demo served by the existing web server (extend `web/server`).
- Bandwidth measurement surfaced in the demo/tests.
- Offline integration tests plus a documented manual demo.

## Key Files

- `src/network/runtime-bridge.ts` — New: event -> runtime/state execution.
- `src/runtime/runtime.ts`, `src/state/state.ts` — Reuse the Demo 9 pipeline (extend if needed).
- `web/server/index.ts` — Add a network demo WebSocket endpoint / host.
- `src/network/__tests__/runtime-bridge.test.ts` — New: integration tests.
- `docs/prd/NETWORK_PRD.md` — Sections 2, 6.4 (runtime integration).

## Constraints

- Reuse Demo 9 runtime/state; do not duplicate playback logic.
- Deterministic playback: the same event stream yields the same sound sequence.
- Keep the network payload under the 1 KB/s budget for the demo stream.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Received behavioural events execute through the Demo 9 runtime/state pipeline.
2. Two clients given the same event stream produce identical playback (same resolved
   sound sequence) - parent AC1.
3. A two-window browser demo served by the existing web server shows synchronised
   host -> client transitions.
4. Measured bandwidth for the demo stream is under 1 KB/s - parent AC2.
5. Offline integration tests plus a documented manual demo; full project test suite
   passes.

## Risky assumptions

- The Demo 9 runtime exposes an API that can execute a received event without side effects
  on local authority; if an adapter seam is missing, it is added minimally.
data.title: Network to Runtime/State integration and two-window demo
